analysis.title: GS Consumer | Morning Trading Update (US)
key_insights: WMT (-1%) reported 3Q with no major surprises or thesis changers. The desk's best guess is the stock finishes lower on the lack of improvement versus last quarter, but expects no large move. Direction of tech flows and risk sentiment likely matters most for staples.
BBWI (-3%) beat 3Q but the Q4 guide is disappointing. WSM reports pre-market, GAP and ROST report tonight, BJ reports tomorrow.

Rates stay in focus. The 10yr yield is back near its highs and the Fed is expected to hike another 25bps in three weeks. This has weighed on retail and discretionary of late, but the market looked through it yesterday with the sector at the top of the leaderboard.
Activity levels are still higher week-to-date, particularly in staples. The desk says fundamental investors want to fade staples the most.

WMT US comps of +2.9% beat consensus by 10 bps but fell just short of a comp bogey of +3% or slightly higher. Improvement versus last quarter was only +30 bps despite pushing through tariff refunds to gain share.

The key debate for WMT is price investments. Last quarter the company said it would lean in heavily on prices, and investor feedback during the quarter was that it backed off that approach. This helped sentiment for Food Retail. Investors are more focused on the WMT read-across for peers than on WMT itself.

WMT 3Q gross margin beat by 30 bps and SG&A missed by 50 bps. By category, grocery was up mid-single digits, Health & Wellness down, General merchandise up low-single digits (toys and auto care strength).

BBWI adjusted operating margin was 7.7% versus 5.6% consensus. Q4 EPS guide of $1.41-1.61 is below the $1.72 consensus. FY revenue guide was raised and FY EPS was reaffirmed. A new $500M buyback was announced.

GAP: GS's Brooke Roach sees mixed tracker signals ahead of 3Q earnings. Physical traffic was volatile, digital engagement stayed positive y/y but moderated in October. Old Navy comp recovery is critical for the stock this quarter.
Americas Gaming October GGR: Virginia +22% y/y, Kansas +2%, Florida -6%. CZR tracking +6% y/y October-to-date, PENN +4%, MGM -1%, BYD +8%.
GS Research roundtable on the impact of AI on travel covered how AI could reshape consumer planning and booking, industry economics, and operational and revenue opportunities.

earnings_insights: WMT 3Q reported 11/19: EPS $0.65 reported vs consensus $0.64, revenue $187.6B vs consensus $187.4B.
WMT 3Q reported: Walmart US comps +2.9% vs consensus +2.8% and expectations for +3-3.2%. Sam's Club comps +4.9% vs consensus +4.8%. Gross margin beat by 30 bps and SG&A missed by 50 bps.
WMT implied 4Q EPS guide of $0.72-$0.77 vs consensus $0.78.

BBWI 3Q reported: adjusted EPS $0.26 vs consensus $0.12, revenue $1.58B vs consensus $1.55B, gross margin 40.5% vs consensus 40.2%, SG&A 33.6% vs consensus 34.5%, adjusted operating margin 7.7% vs consensus 5.6%.

BBWI Q4 guide: EPS $1.41-1.61 vs consensus $1.72, revenue -5.5% to -2.0% vs consensus -2.1%. FY revenue guide raised to -3.4% to -2.1% (vs consensus -2.5% and prior -4% to -2.5%). Adjusted FY EPS reaffirmed at $2.60-2.80 vs consensus $2.70. New $500M buyback. Conference call at 8:30am.
Upcoming earnings: WSM reports pre-market 11/19, GAP and ROST report after the close 11/19, BJ reports 11/20.
